faqs.q: What is the national minimum wage in Australia for 2026-27?
faqs.a: From 1 July 2026, the National Minimum Wage is $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.90 per week for a 38-hour week. Casual employees receive an additional 25% loading, making the minimum casual rate $33.05 per hour. These rates are set by the Fair Work Commission.

bodyMarkdown:
## What is Australia's minimum wage? Understanding hourly to annual pay

If you've ever wondered **what is Australia's minimum wage** and how it translates to an annual salary, you're in the right place. This guide explains the conversion from hourly rates to yearly pay, covering the National Minimum Wage, award rates, casual loading, superannuation, and tax. We'll also look at state differences in ordinary-time earnings and how to use our [the timesheet](/) calculator to estimate your take-home pay.

### How to convert your hourly rate to an annual salary

The basic formula is straightforward: multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work each week, then multiply by 52 weeks in a year. For a standard full-time role, we assume a 38-hour week as defined by the Fair Work Ombudsman. So:

**Annual gross pay ≈ hourly rate × 38 hours × 52 weeks**

For example, at the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour (from 1 July 2026), the annual gross salary is approximately $52,261.44 before tax and super. If you work fewer or more hours, adjust the weekly hours accordingly. Our [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) page has more details.

It's also helpful to think in fortnightly terms. Your weekly pay is hourly × 38, and your fortnightly pay is simply that amount doubled. For the minimum wage, that's $1,004.90 per week or $2,009.80 per fortnight.

### National Minimum Wage vs award rates

The National Minimum Wage is the legal minimum for all employees not covered by an award or agreement. As of 1 July 2026, it is $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.90 per week for 38 hours. However, most employees are covered by a modern award or enterprise agreement that sets higher minimum rates for their industry or role. The Fair Work Commission reviews the National Minimum Wage annually, but award rates can vary significantly.

Casual employees receive a 25% loading on top of the base rate to compensate for lack of paid leave. So the minimum casual rate is $33.05 per hour. When using our [the timesheet](/) calculator, enter your base hourly rate (without casual loading) and check the "casual loading" box to add 25% automatically. Never enter a rate that already includes the loading.

Superannuation guarantee is paid on top of your ordinary earnings. From 1 July 2026, the super rate is 12% of your ordinary time earnings, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year. This means your employer contributes an additional amount to your super fund, which is not deducted from your salary. For more on this, see our [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) page.

### State differences in ordinary-time earnings

While the National Minimum Wage applies across Australia, average weekly earnings vary by state and territory. According to the Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS) Average Weekly Earnings survey for May 2026, full-time adult ordinary time earnings nationally were $2,083.70 per week. However, states like New South Wales, Victoria, and Western Australia often report higher averages due to industry mix and cost of living, while others may be lower.

It's important to note that these are averages across all industries and occupations, not a median for any specific job. If you're looking for pay information for a particular role, check relevant award rates or use our [average pay](/topics/average-pay) page for national and state-level data. The ABS also publishes detailed earnings by state and industry, which can give you a better picture of what's typical in your area.

### Using the timesheet calculator

Our [the timesheet](/) tool is designed to help you quickly estimate your annual, fortnightly, and weekly pay, along with tax and super. Here's how to use it:

1. Enter your base hourly rate (the rate before any casual loading).
2. If you are a casual employee, check the "25% casual loading" box. The calculator will add the loading automatically.
3. The calculator assumes a 38-hour week, but you can adjust the hours if you work part-time or different hours.
4. It then shows your gross annual salary, weekly and fortnightly amounts, estimated tax (using the 2026-27 resident tax rates), Medicare levy (2%), and superannuation (12% on top).

Remember, this is an estimate. It assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. For a more detailed breakdown, see our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) page.

### Tax and super considerations for 2026-27

The Australian Taxation Office (ATO) sets the resident tax rates for 2026-27 as follows:
- $0 – $18,200: nil
- $18,201 – $45,000: 15c for each $1 over $18,200
- $45,001 – $135,000: $4,020 plus 30c for each $1 over $45,000
- $135,001 – $190,000: $31,020 plus 37c for each $1 over $135,000
- $190,001 and over: $51,370 plus 45c for each $1 over $190,000

Plus a Medicare levy of 2% (with possible reductions for low-income earners). The 2025-26 single reduction thresholds are used here as the 2026-27 thresholds were not confirmed at the time of this guide. HELP repayments, Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not included in this estimate.

Superannuation is calculated at 12% of your ordinary time earnings, paid on top by your employer. The maximum contribution base for the super guarantee is $270,830 per year, meaning super is only payable on earnings up to that amount.

### Important disclaimers

The annual pay shown here is hourly rate × hours per week × 52. It assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax is the 2026-27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025-26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026-27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.

For more detailed information, refer to the Fair Work Ombudsman for pay rates, the Australian Taxation Office for tax, and the Australian Bureau of Statistics for earnings data. You can also explore our [reference tables](/data) for quick lookups.
